title: How do airplanes actually fly? - Raymond Adkins
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】飛機實際上是如何飛行的？ ——雷蒙德‧阿德金斯（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: By 1917, Albert Einstein had explained the relationship between space and time.
cues.en: By 1917, Albert Einstein had explained the relationship between space and time.
cues.zh: 到了 1917 年時， 亞伯特‧愛因斯坦已經解釋了 空間和時間之間的關係。

cues.text: But, that year, he designed a flawed airplane wing.
cues.en: But, that year, he designed a flawed airplane wing.
cues.zh: 但那一年，他設計出了 有問題的機翼。

cues.text: His attempt was based on an incomplete theory of flight.
cues.en: His attempt was based on an incomplete theory of flight.
cues.zh: 但那一年，他設計出了 有問題的機翼。 他嘗試的做法是以一個 不完整的飛行理論為依據。

cues.text: Indeed, insufficient and inaccurate explanations still circulate today.
cues.en: Indeed, insufficient and inaccurate explanations still circulate today.
cues.zh: 的確，不充份和不正確的解釋 現今仍然在流傳著。

cues.text: So, where did Einstein go wrong?
cues.en: So, where did Einstein go wrong?
cues.zh: 那麼，愛因斯坦錯在哪裡？

cues.text: And how do planes fly?
cues.en: And how do planes fly?
cues.zh: 飛機又是怎麼飛起來的？

cues.text: Though we don’t always think of it this way, air is a fluid medium—
cues.en: Though we don’t always think of it this way, air is a fluid medium—
cues.zh: 雖然我們不見得都用這種角度思考， 但空氣是一種流體介質——

cues.text: it’s just less dense than liquids like water.
cues.en: it’s just less dense than liquids like water.
cues.zh: 只是它的密度比水這類液體還要低。

cues.text: Things that are lighter than air are buoyant within it, while heavier objects require an upward force, called lift, to stay aloft.
cues.en: Things that are lighter than air are buoyant within it, while heavier objects require an upward force, called lift, to stay aloft.
cues.zh: 比空氣輕的東西會浮在空氣中， 而較重的東西則需要向上的力量， 稱為升力，才能持續留在空中。

cues.text: For planes, this force is mostly generated by the wings.
cues.en: For planes, this force is mostly generated by the wings.
cues.zh: 就飛機來說，升力 多半是由機翼產生。

cues.text: One especially pervasive false description of lift is the “Longer Path” or “Equal Transit Time” explanation.
cues.en: One especially pervasive false description of lift is the “Longer Path” or “Equal Transit Time” explanation.
cues.zh: 關於升力，最普遍的錯誤說法之一 是「更長的路徑」 或「相等透過時間」這套解釋。

cues.text: It states that air molecules traveling over the top of a curved wing
cues.en: It states that air molecules traveling over the top of a curved wing
cues.zh: 這個說法是：空氣分子從 有弧度的機翼上方流過，

cues.text: cover a longer distance than those traveling underneath.
cues.en: cover a longer distance than those traveling underneath.
cues.zh: 要行經的距離 比從下方流過的分子更長。

cues.text: For the air molecules above to reach the wing’s trailing edge
cues.en: For the air molecules above to reach the wing’s trailing edge
cues.zh: 從上方流過的分子 要抵達機翼的後緣， 且要和被機翼分開而從下方 透過的分子同時抵達，

cues.text: in the same instance as those that split off and went below,
cues.en: in the same instance as those that split off and went below,
cues.zh: 且要和被機翼分開而從下方 透過的分子同時抵達，

cues.text: air must travel faster above, creating a pocket of lower pressure that lifts the plane.
cues.en: air must travel faster above, creating a pocket of lower pressure that lifts the plane.
cues.zh: 且要和被機翼分開而從下方 透過的分子同時抵達， 上面的空氣一定得 以更快的速度行進， 創造出一個壓力較低的 空間，讓飛機被抬起。

cues.text: This explanation has been thoroughly debunked.
cues.en: This explanation has been thoroughly debunked.
cues.zh: 這個解釋已經被完全拆穿了。

cues.text: Air molecules floating above and below the wing don't need to meet back up.
cues.en: Air molecules floating above and below the wing don't need to meet back up.
cues.zh: 從機翼上方和下方透過的空氣分子 並不需要再相會。

cues.text: In reality, the air traveling above reaches the wing’s trailing edge
cues.en: In reality, the air traveling above reaches the wing’s trailing edge
cues.zh: 實際上，從上方透過的 空氣分子抵達機翼後緣的時間 會比下方的空氣早許多。

cues.text: much faster than the air beneath.
cues.en: much faster than the air beneath.
cues.zh: 會比下方的空氣早許多。

cues.text: To get a sense of how lift is actually generated, let's simulate an airplane wing in motion.
cues.en: To get a sense of how lift is actually generated, let's simulate an airplane wing in motion.
cues.zh: 為了了解升力實際上是如何產生的， 咱們來模擬飛行中的機翼。

cues.text: As it moves forward, the wing affects the movement of the air around it.
cues.en: As it moves forward, the wing affects the movement of the air around it.
cues.zh: 機翼向前移動時， 會影響其周圍空氣的移動。

cues.text: As air meets the wing’s solid surface, a thin layer sticks to the wing.
cues.en: As air meets the wing’s solid surface, a thin layer sticks to the wing.
cues.zh: 在空氣碰到機翼的堅固表面時， 會有薄薄一層空氣附著在機翼上。

cues.text: This layer pulls the surrounding air with it.
cues.en: This layer pulls the surrounding air with it.
cues.zh: 這一層會將周遭的空氣朝它拉過去。

cues.text: The air splits into pathways above and below the wing,
cues.en: The air splits into pathways above and below the wing,
cues.zh: 空氣會分成兩路， 分別從機翼的上方和下方

cues.text: following the wing’s contour.
cues.en: following the wing’s contour.
cues.zh: 沿著機翼的外輪廓透過。

cues.text: As the air that’s routed above makes its way around the nose of the wing,
cues.en: As the air that’s routed above makes its way around the nose of the wing,
cues.zh: 當上方的空氣沿著機翼前緣透過時，

cues.text: it experiences centripetal acceleration, the force you also feel in a sharply turning car.
cues.en: it experiences centripetal acceleration, the force you also feel in a sharply turning car.
cues.zh: 會發生向心加速。 也就是坐在急轉彎的車上 會感受到的那股力量。

cues.text: The air above therefore gathers more speed than the air traveling below.
cues.en: The air above therefore gathers more speed than the air traveling below.
cues.zh: 因此上方空氣的移動速度 會比下方空氣更快。

cues.text: This increased speed is coupled with a decrease in pressure above the wing,
cues.en: This increased speed is coupled with a decrease in pressure above the wing,
cues.zh: 而速度提升也會伴隨著 機翼上方的壓力下降，

cues.text: which pulls even more air across the wing’s upper surface.
cues.en: which pulls even more air across the wing’s upper surface.
cues.zh: 導致更多空氣從機翼上方流過。

cues.text: The air flowing across the lower surface, meanwhile, experiences less of a change in direction and speed.
cues.en: The air flowing across the lower surface, meanwhile, experiences less of a change in direction and speed.
cues.zh: 同時，從下方流過的空氣 相對沒有那麼多方向和速度的改變。

cues.text: The pressure across the wing’s lower surface is thus higher than that above the upper surface.
cues.en: The pressure across the wing’s lower surface is thus higher than that above the upper surface.
cues.zh: 因此，機翼下方的壓力會較高， 比上方的壓力還高。

cues.text: This pressure difference results in the upwards force of lift.
cues.en: This pressure difference results in the upwards force of lift.
cues.zh: 這種壓力差造成向上的升力。

cues.text: The faster the plane travels, the greater the pressure difference, and the greater that force.
cues.en: The faster the plane travels, the greater the pressure difference, and the greater that force.
cues.zh: 飛機飛得越快， 壓力差就會越大，升力也就會越大。

cues.text: Once it overcomes the downward force of gravity, the plane takes off.
cues.en: Once it overcomes the downward force of gravity, the plane takes off.
cues.zh: 壓力差就會越大，升力也就會越大。 一旦升力大於向下的重力， 飛機就能起飛了。

cues.text: Air flows smoothly around curved wings.
cues.en: Air flows smoothly around curved wings.
cues.zh: 空氣會平順地沿著機翼的弧線流動，

cues.text: But a wing’s curvature is not the cause of lift.
cues.en: But a wing’s curvature is not the cause of lift.
cues.zh: 但升力並非機翼的弧度所造成。

cues.text: In fact, a flat wing that’s tilted upwards can also create lift—
cues.en: In fact, a flat wing that’s tilted upwards can also create lift—
cues.zh: 事實上，將平的機翼向前傾斜 也能創造出升力，

cues.text: as long as the air bends around it, contributing to and reinforcing the pressure difference.
cues.en: as long as the air bends around it, contributing to and reinforcing the pressure difference.
cues.zh: 也能創造出升力， 只要空氣會因為它而彎曲， 造成和強化壓力差，即可。

cues.text: Meanwhile, having a wing that’s too curved or steeply angled
cues.en: Meanwhile, having a wing that’s too curved or steeply angled
cues.zh: 而如果機翼的弧度太大或角度太陡，

cues.text: can be disastrous: the airflow above may detach from the wing and become turbulent.
cues.en: can be disastrous: the airflow above may detach from the wing and become turbulent.
cues.zh: 可能會造成災難： 機翼上方的氣流可能會 與機翼分離，變成亂流。

cues.text: This is probably what happened with Einstein’s wing design,
cues.en: This is probably what happened with Einstein’s wing design,
cues.zh: 愛因斯坦設計的機翼 可能就有這個問題，

cues.text: nicknamed “the cat’s back.” By increasing the wing’s curvature,
cues.en: nicknamed “the cat’s back.” By increasing the wing’s curvature,
cues.zh: 他把這個設計暱稱為「貓背」。 之所以增加機翼的弧度，

cues.text: Einstein thought it would generate more lift.
cues.en: Einstein thought it would generate more lift.
cues.zh: 之所以增加機翼的弧度， 是因為愛因斯坦認為 這樣能產生更多升力。 但一名測試飛行員回報說 飛機飛起來很不穩，

cues.text: But one test pilot reported that the plane wobbled like “a pregnant duck” in flight.
cues.en: But one test pilot reported that the plane wobbled like “a pregnant duck” in flight.
cues.zh: 但一名測試飛行員回報說 飛機飛起來很不穩， 就像是「懷孕的鴨子在飛」。

cues.text: Our explanation is still a simplified description of this nuanced, complex process.
cues.en: Our explanation is still a simplified description of this nuanced, complex process.
cues.zh: 我們的解釋其實也只是簡單描述 這個精密又複雜的過程。

cues.text: Other factors, like the air that’s flowing meters beyond the wing’s surface—
cues.en: Other factors, like the air that’s flowing meters beyond the wing’s surface—
cues.zh: 其他因素，比如在距離機翼 數公尺外流動的空氣——

cues.text: being swept up, then down— as well as air vortices formed at the wing’s tips,
cues.en: being swept up, then down— as well as air vortices formed at the wing’s tips,
cues.zh: 其他因素，比如在距離機翼 數公尺外流動的空氣—— 先被捲向上，之後又下降—— 還有在機翼尖端附近形成的氣旋，

cues.text: all influence lift.
cues.en: all influence lift.
cues.zh: 還有在機翼尖端附近形成的氣旋， 都會影響升力。

cues.text: And, while experts agree that the pressure difference generates lift,
cues.en: And, while experts agree that the pressure difference generates lift,
cues.zh: 且，雖然專家都認同 壓力差會產生升力，

cues.text: their explanations for how can vary.
cues.en: their explanations for how can vary.
cues.zh: 對於如何產生，卻眾說紛雲。

cues.text: Some might emphasize the air’s behavior at the wing’s surface,
cues.en: Some might emphasize the air’s behavior at the wing’s surface,
cues.zh: 有些人強調機翼表面空氣的變化，

cues.text: others the upward force created as the air is deflected downwards.
cues.en: others the upward force created as the air is deflected downwards.
cues.zh: 有些人強調機翼表面空氣的變化， 其他人則著重空氣被迫轉向 向下時產生出的向上升力。

cues.text: However, there's no controversy when it comes to the math.
cues.en: However, there's no controversy when it comes to the math.
cues.zh: 但是，在數學上是沒有爭議的。

cues.text: Engineers use a set of formulas called the Navier-Stokes equations
cues.en: Engineers use a set of formulas called the Navier-Stokes equations
cues.zh: 工程師們用一組方程式， 即「納維爾—史托克方程式」，

cues.text: to precisely model air’s flow around a wing and detail how lift is generated.
cues.en: to precisely model air’s flow around a wing and detail how lift is generated.
cues.zh: 來精確建立出機翼周圍的氣流模型， 並詳細說明升力是如何產生的。

cues.text: More than a century after Einstein’s foray into aeronautics,
cues.en: More than a century after Einstein’s foray into aeronautics,
cues.zh: 在愛因斯坦初次涉足 航空學的一個世紀多之後，

cues.text: lift retains its reputation as a confounding concept.
cues.en: lift retains its reputation as a confounding concept.
cues.zh: 在愛因斯坦初次涉足 航空學的一個世紀多之後， 升力仍然保有 「困惑人的觀念」這名聲。

cues.text: But when it feels like it’s all going to come crashing down, remember:
cues.en: But when it feels like it’s all going to come crashing down, remember:
cues.zh: 但在感覺好像要墜機時，別忘了：

cues.text: it’s just the physics of fluid in motion.
cues.en: it’s just the physics of fluid in motion.
cues.zh: 這只是流體物理學在發揮作用而已。

cues.en: This video was made possible with support from Marriott Hotels.

cues.text: With over 590 hotels and resorts across the globe,
cues.en: With over 590 hotels and resorts across the globe,
cues.zh: 在全球各地有超過 590 家 旅館和渡假飯店，

cues.text: Marriott Hotels celebrates the curiosity that propels us to travel.
cues.en: Marriott Hotels celebrates the curiosity that propels us to travel.
cues.zh: 萬豪酒店讚頌的是 促使我們去旅行的好奇心。

cues.text: Check out some of the exciting ways TED-Ed and Marriott are working together,
cues.en: Check out some of the exciting ways TED-Ed and Marriott are working together,
cues.zh: 來看看 TED-Ed 和萬豪酒店 一些讓人興奮的合作方式，

cues.text: and book your next journey at Marriott Hotels.
cues.en: and book your next journey at Marriott Hotels.
